reported_success.quote: We were able to reproduce and replicate this similarity effect with the original sample and a new sample. [...] However, when using a polynomial regression and response surface approach, a similarity effect between the present and future self did not emerge—neither in the original sample (Study 1) nor in the new sample (Study 2).

notes: Primary-source titles and DOIs verified in the acquired full texts. Original supplied locator p. 2 describes methods; target statistics are on p. 3, Table 2. Replication supplied locator p. 9 contains discussion/response-surface figure; the difference-score regression is on PDF p. 8, Table 9. Study 2 uses concurrent, adjusted student life-satisfaction items rather than life satisfaction 10 years later; target_match is false for this known outcome/time mismatch. Model 2 replication controls age and gender only, whereas original Model 2 also controls income and education. Replication beta is retained at the .302 precision printed in prose (Table 9 rounds it to .30); p comes from the same regression in Table 9. Success label captures the authors’ replication of the difference-score association and their explicit methodological critique. Quotes normalize PDF extraction artifacts for mathematical symbols and line breaks; bracketed ellipsis separates passages.
